image.description: 華航Airbus A350-900同型機資料照片，圖中為B-18915，非本文所述前四川航空航機，亦非其客艙照片。

zh.title: 華航前四川航空A350補強運能　331席客艙、服務差異與改裝安排解析
zh.summary: 華航引進前四川航空A350，背景涉及航網需求與新機交付延遲；新增運能與客艙升級卻有不同時程。官方B-18920座位圖顯示331席、兩艙等配置，與原有306席版本不同，而三架A350另有客艙設備升級公告。
body: 中華航空引進前四川航空Airbus A350-900，增加可調度的廣體客機，但同一個A350機型名稱之下，旅客實際遇到的客艙並不完全相同。這批航機的加入，涉及運能補強、原有座艙配置與後續升級等不同階段；飛機換上華航塗裝並投入服務，並不表示座椅、娛樂設備及機上網路已全部換成華航原有A350的產品規格。
為何引進已有營運履歷的飛機？華航2025年年報在未來營運計畫中，將增購三架A350-900與航網規劃需求、交機延遲狀況連結，並提到以提高航機使用率、延長租期及評估增租等方式穩定運能。從這項官方說明來看，接收可取得的既有航機，是補足運能的一環；不能只用全新或二手，就完整解釋這筆機隊決策。
從交易關係來看，四川航空是這批航機的前營運者，華航此次購機的交易對象則是ILFC Ireland Limited。華航年報將雙方簽訂的三架A350-900交易列為購機契約，2026年3月補充公告也使用購價總額的表述。這是既有Airbus航機轉換營運者的機隊交易；評估引進效益時，應回到可用運能、交付條件與後續整備，而飛機過去在哪個國家服役，本身不足以判斷現在的客艙品質。
內裝最明確的差異，先看得到的座位配置。華航官方以B-18920標示的座艙圖，列有28席豪華商務艙、303席經濟艙，合計331席，沒有豪華經濟艙；商務艙採1-2-1、經濟艙採3-3-3排列。相較之下，華航原有306席A350配置為32席豪華商務艙、31席豪華經濟艙及243席經濟艙。兩者總席數相差25席，但其中也包含艙等比例改變，不能僅憑總席數就認定每個座位都更窄。
B-18920官方座位圖進一步標示，商務艙座椅可180度平躺、平躺長度75吋，經濟艙椅距31至32吋，個人螢幕分別為15.4吋及10.6吋。這些規格能說明硬體差別，卻不能代替實際座椅狀況、清潔與維護表現，也不能把單一機號的圖表當作所有航機每一項設備都相同的證明。旅客比較產品時，應查看該航班實際選位圖與艙等供應，而非只看訂位頁的A350名稱。
機上網路則是另一個需要獨立確認的項目。華航Wi-Fi頁面明列特定A350航機暫無提供服務，免費傳訊或免費瀏覽的資格，也都以實際有提供Wi-Fi為前提。另一方面，洗手間、座椅與影音設備能否正常使用，屬於日常客艙維護及服務管理的要求；全面換新客艙的工程尚未完成，並不能取代對既有設備可用狀況的管理。從服務品質角度，增加航班運能與維持客艙設施正常，兩者都需要兼顧。

後續升級並非沒有規劃。華航在2026年5月8日公告三架A350-900客艙設備升級案，總金額上限1.23億美元，交易對象包括Airbus、Airbus Atlantic、Recaro及RAVE Aerospace，目的為升級客艙設備與品質。不過，這份公告沒有逐一列出機號、各機進廠日期與完工日；它可以證明三架升級案已獲董事會通過，不能據此寫成本文提及的每架航機都已改裝完畢，或保證某個航班會使用新客艙。
此外，華航2024年公布的原有15架A350改艙計畫，預計2027年起推出新客艙、2028年完成15架工程，內容涵蓋座椅、娛樂系統、機上網路與客艙環境。這項較早公布的15架計畫，與後來另行公告的三架升級案，必須分別閱讀，不能直接套用同一個逐架完工時程。對旅客最有意義的，仍是購票時能辨識產品差異、搭機時設備正常，以及改裝完成後有清楚可核對的上線資訊。

en.title: China Airlines’ Ex-Sichuan A350s Add Capacity While Cabin Products and Upgrade Timelines Differ
en.summary: China Airlines links three additional A350-900s to network needs and delivery delays. Its B-18920 seat map shows 331 seats in two classes, unlike the original 306-seat product. A separate three-aircraft cabin-upgrade disclosure establishes a project, not completed refurbishment.
body: China Airlines’ introduction of Airbus A350-900s formerly operated by Sichuan Airlines adds widebody capacity, but does not make every A350 cabin identical. Fleet entry, the retained seating layout and subsequent product upgrades are separate stages. China Airlines branding alone does not establish that seats, entertainment and connectivity have all been converted to its original A350 specifications.

The airline’s 2025 annual report connects the planned acquisition of three A350-900s with network requirements and aircraft-delivery delays. It also describes improving utilisation, extending leases and evaluating additional leased capacity to stabilise operations. The acquisition should therefore be understood as part of a capacity response, rather than explained solely by whether aircraft are new or previously operated.

Sichuan Airlines was the previous operator, while China Airlines’ annual report identifies ILFC Ireland Limited as the counterparty for the three-aircraft purchase contract. A March 2026 disclosure also refers to a purchase price. This is a fleet transaction involving existing Airbus aircraft changing operators. Available capacity, delivery conditions and subsequent preparation are relevant considerations; the former operating country alone does not establish present cabin quality.

China Airlines’ official seat map labelled B-18920 shows 28 Premium Business and 303 Economy seats: 331 in total, without Premium Economy. Business seating is arranged 1-2-1 and Economy 3-3-3. The original 306-seat product instead has 32 Premium Business, 31 Premium Economy and 243 Economy seats. The 25-seat difference includes a change in cabin mix and does not itself prove that every seat is narrower.

The B-18920 map specifies 180-degree flat-bed Business seats with a 75-inch bed length, Economy pitch of 31–32 inches, and respective entertainment screens of 15.4 and 10.6 inches. Specifications do not establish actual upkeep, cleanliness or every other aircraft’s equipment. Passengers should compare the seat map and cabins offered on their particular flight.

Connectivity requires a separate check: China Airlines explicitly excludes certain A350s from its Wi-Fi service. Complimentary-access benefits apply only where service exists. Working lavatories, seats and entertainment systems are also everyday cabin-maintenance and service expectations. A future refurbishment project does not replace management of the equipment already offered to passengers.

On May 8, 2026, China Airlines disclosed a three-A350 cabin-equipment upgrade with a US$123 million ceiling, involving Airbus, Airbus Atlantic, Recaro and RAVE Aerospace. The disclosure establishes board approval for an upgrade project, but does not list individual registrations, induction dates or completion dates. It cannot establish that every aircraft discussed here has already been refurbished or guarantee a new cabin on a specific flight.

Separately, the airline’s 2024 announcement covered 15 existing A350s, with new cabins planned from 2027 and completion of that programme targeted for 2028. It included seats, entertainment, connectivity and cabin surroundings. Those dates should not automatically be applied to every aircraft in the later three-aircraft disclosure. Clear product information, functioning facilities and verifiable entry-into-service updates remain the most useful benchmarks for passengers.
